How big is big data visualized as printed paper
recent_posts.summary: A visual demonstration of big data scale by physically printing database rows on paper. Starting from 50 rows per page, the comparison scales up: 1,000 rows is 20 pages, a million rows is 20,000 sheets (2 meters tall), and a billion rows would be 2 km of paper — taller than any building in Canada. PostgreSQL can query a million rows instantly, while Spotify generates a trillion events per day. The video is sponsored by Supabase, which offers PostgreSQL with real-time storage and auto-generated APIs.

recent_posts.title: What a billion database rows look like as physical paper
recent_posts.summary: A visual and conceptual exploration of what database scale looks like in physical terms. Starting from 50 rows on a single sheet of paper, the post scales up to a billion rows — equivalent to a two-kilometer-tall stack — and compares that to real-world data volumes from Spotify, Uber, and Facebook. Along the way, it explains core database concepts like indexes and joins using paper-stack analogies, illustrating why Postgres can retrieve a single row from billions in milliseconds. The post is sponsored by Supabase.

recent_posts.title: The Humble History of 7Zip
recent_posts.summary: 7-Zip is a free, open-source file compression tool created by a single developer, Igor Pavlov, in 1999. Its custom LZMA compression algorithm achieves 30–70% better compression than ZIP and has been adopted widely across Linux, Android, and game installers. Despite its dated Windows XP-era UI, it remains universally trusted and has been maintained for over 25 years at no cost, outperforming commercial alternatives like WinRAR.

recent_posts.title: How attackers exploit GitHub trending with fake stars and hidden malware
recent_posts.summary: GitHub's trending page is being exploited by attackers who create repositories with legitimate-sounding names and purchase fake stars to lure developers into downloading malware. Researchers built Star Scout, which scanned six years of GitHub metadata and identified over 6 million suspicious fake stars by detecting ghost accounts and coordinated starring clusters. One group called Banana Squad published nearly 70 repos mimicking real Python security tools, hiding malicious code by padding it with hundreds of blank spaces to push it off-screen. A separate campaign compromised a single GitHub Action and put over 23,000 repositories at risk. The open source ecosystem's trust model is being systematically exploited at scale.

recent_posts.title: Five developer workflows you can automate with AI today
recent_posts.summary: Five developer workflow automations enabled by AI: automatic ticket creation from incidents, incident summarization to catch up quickly, self-service answers from internal docs, smart ticket routing to the right team, and change risk analysis that flags potentially breaking deploys based on historical patterns. ServiceNow's AI platform is presented as the solution delivering these capabilities.

recent_posts.title: Axios npm account hijacked in supply chain attack installing remote access trojan
recent_posts.summary: The Axios JavaScript library, installed over 300 million times per week, was compromised in a supply chain attack. An attacker hijacked a lead maintainer's npm account, changed the email address, and published two malicious versions. Rather than injecting malicious code directly, the attacker added a dependency that ran a postinstall script installing a Remote Access Trojan on victim machines. The attack bypassed CI/CD pipelines entirely. Given Axios installs at ~500 times per second, even a short exposure window could have compromised a significant number of machines. The attack was caught relatively quickly but highlights the danger of supply chain vulnerabilities in widely-used open source packages.

recent_posts.title: How Google Maps uses graph neural networks to predict traffic
recent_posts.summary: Google Maps predicts traffic before it happens by combining real-time GPS data from millions of users with historical traffic patterns. After acquiring Waze for $1.1 billion in 2013, Google enriched its data further. The system uses graph neural networks that split roads into 'super segments' and process terabytes of traffic data to forecast slowdowns before they occur, achieving 97% accuracy.

recent_posts.title: How YouTube encodes and streams video at massive scale
recent_posts.summary: YouTube receives 500 hours of video uploads every minute. Each uploaded video is encoded into multiple versions across different resolutions (240p to 4K) and codecs. All videos get encoded to H.264 by default, but high-traffic videos are also encoded in AV1, which offers smaller file sizes for easier web transmission. Adaptive bitrate streaming dynamically switches between quality levels based on the viewer's internet speed, which explains why videos sometimes appear blurry. A single uploaded video results in dozens of stored variants that are seamlessly swapped depending on conditions.
